steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Mix ground beef, bread crumbs, onion, water, and egg together in a large bowl just until combined. Shape into small meatballs, about 1 ¼ inches wide, and arrange on a nonstick baking sheet with space between them. Bake in the preheated oven for 20 to 25 minutes, turning once, until browned and an instant-read thermometer inserted into the centers reads 160 degrees F (71 degrees C).
Stir cranberry sauce, chili sauce, brown sugar, and lemon juice together in a large saucepan over low heat until smooth. Add meatballs and simmer gently for 1 hour, stirring occasionally.
Serve warm, or transfer the meatballs and sauce to a slow cooker set to Warm so guests can help themselves.

raw_recipe.headline: Cocktail Meatballs
raw_recipe.description: Make homemade cocktail meatballs simmered in a sweet-tangy cranberry sauce for an easy holiday or party appetizer.

review.reviewBody:
These meatballs were a hit! I used frozen meatballs.
Most jellied cranberry sauce come in 16 oz cans so if you decide to use the whole can you'll need to double all the other ingredients. Typical chili sauce comes in 12oz. bottle so you'll need two bottles if you use the full can of cranberry. Hope this helps your shopping.

I have made these numerous times and am ashamed to admit I'm just now reviewing them. Wonderful addition to the regular grape jelly recipes out there with great meatballs.... Based on experience and personal preference with these cocktail meatballs I offer the following suggestions: 1.) Add one packet of lipton onion soup mix to the meatball mixture if you do not have time to mince or grate the onion. 2.) Bake meatballs over a drip pan to reduce the fat before adding to the sauce. 3.) If using frozen meatballs ENSURE you DO NOT use Italian meatballs as this upsets the balance of the meatballs and sauce (yuck)! 3.) Make the sauce the day before to let the flavors marry - I can't stress what a difference this makes! This recipe gets better the next day. 4.) The Heinz sauce in the round bottle seems to be the best chili sauce for this mixture. Reviewers: I seriously dislike people that rate a recipe based on the changes they have made to the original. I want to state that I rated this recipe on the recipe Lara submitted. The changes I suggested were based on my family's personal preference. Thanks Lara for a fabulous appetizer recipe - I always give you the credit!

These were great. A huge hit with my family. The only thing I did differently was substitute 1 packet of lipton onion soup for the minced onion. It added great flavor. My nephews couldn't get enough of these meatballs. I highly recommend this recipe.

This is a very tasty recipe for meatballs, with the cranberry sauce representing a change from the run of the mill grape jelly recipe. I used seasoned bread crumbs, which added some nice flavor to the meatballs, and then baked them on a broiler tray, which allowed the fat to run off while they were baking. One recipe is enough to fill one of the small 1 to 2 quart crockpots. I made the meatballs 2 days ahead, and refrigerated them. The day of my party, I made the sauce, put the meatballs in the crockpot, added the sauce, and put the whole crock back in the fridge. About 2 hours before the party, I put the crock back in the warmer, and plugged it in. Voila! Easy and tasty. I was so impressed with the recipe, that I made an extra batch of the meatballs, and froze them. I will use them for another party in the next couple of weeks. I'll bet you could use ground turkey for a little less fat. Thanks for sharing a wonderful recipe!

Fromrfjl46
I have been making these meatballs for 30 years or more in my catering business. I however use cornflakes crumbs instead of bread crumbs. I also put 1/3 cup parsley; I use 1/4 cup ketchup instead of water and 1 tsp. soy sauce. Just a tought from an old chef
Made these. Only adjustment I made was to add a few oz of bourbon. Im from Kentucky, we add bourbon to everything lol.... Great hit at party.

Fantastic! Only change I made is to use Lipton Onion Soup Mix, rather than chopped onion as suggested by other reviewers. I doubled this recipe and got 46 meatballs from two pounds of ground beef. With a pasta casserole, three adults polished off 30 meatballs for dinner! I'm definitely making this again. It's extremely easy to make, not overly sweet, and the meatballs hold together very well. I cooked them on high in the pressure cooker (cold from fridge as I made the meatballs and sauce the night before) for about two hours. If you're going to make them for a party, I'd switch to low or keep warm after 2 to 3 hours depending on how hot your slow cooker runs. For reference, I made these in a 7 quart slow cooker and I think for that size slow cooker, you could easily use 5 to 6 lbs of meat. If you plan on making these for a party, I recommend making the meatballs in advance, freeze them, and then defrost before using to save time. Great recipe for dinner, potlucks, or parties.
Meatballs were so tasty with the sauce. I shredded some gruyere cheese on the meatballs and had some Hawaiian sweet rolls and made a few sliders that were delicious.

Absolutely love this recipe!! These meatballs are a huge hit every time I make them, dinner, snack, potlucks, everything! I have tried both frozen meatballs and handmade and definitely prefer handmade, it does not taste the same! We also started cooking our meatballs in the air fryer instead of the oven, they come out perfect every time. 12 minutes at 360°, shake them a couple times while cooking and voila! We have also browned them in a skillet but the air fryer is the win and makes for easy cleanup. You will not go wrong with this recipe!!

Made this for my father's 90th birthday celebration. Because the party was put together on fairly short notice, I looked for an easy, yet good appetizer to bring. Worked like a charm. As others have mentioned, I did use Armour (non-Italian) meatballs; otherwise I used the recipe as stated. They were a big hit. Everyone wanted to know what I did. As others have mentioned, because there was a large group attending, I got 3 bags of frozen meatballs, used a full can of the cranberry jelly, 2 bottles of Heinz "Chili Sauce", and doubled the other ingredients. Just mixed them all together in Crock Pot for a couple hours ahead and was done. Will be using again, for sure!

I love this recipe! The meatballs came out great. The only thing I changed was instead of water I used milk. I always have used milk when making meatballs. It was easy to put together ahead of time . I used a crock pot to keep them warm. It was a great addition to our football party!🏈

Have been enjoying this treat for more than 70 years. I make my own meatballs, as I prefer them to be little--a single bite. I always multiply the recipe by 3 and have plenty of them in my freezer. When I was a child, the sauce was made with grape jelly and chili sauce--I like this cranberry version better. I also like to use half lean ground beef and half ground pork--and have done them that way for about 60 years since I set up my own household. I also love using ground chicken!

Holy hotness! Luckily, I only had half the amount of chili sauce, but even using that, my family had tears running down their face. Spiciness isn’t the sole issue, though…It literally tasted like meatballs covered in spicy chili sauce. If I had an extra can of cranberry on hand, I probably could’ve saved it, but I didn’t, so it was a disaster
Luscious aroma wafts scross the room when served. Irresistible!

I have been making this recipe for almost 50 years, using the wrong type of canned cranberry ingredient. My recipe called for Whole Berry Cranberry Sauce. Everything else was the same. I love it now with the smooth Jellied Cranberry Sauce, as this recipe calls for. What a difference a simple can of cranberry sauce can make!! Thank you to the Allrecipes Member who improved this great recipe!

Same recipe as I have used in the past, but I prefer putting the raw meatballs in a glass pan and pouring the heated up sauce over the meatballs and cooking it that way. I also felt it really needed salt. I added some twice after mixed together, but stll tasted a little bland. I threw a little Siracha sauce in it to make it hotter.
I followed the recipe exactly. I thought it was good. The only change I would make is a little less bread crumbs.
Went with grape jelly instead of cranberry. Still great
Didn't change a thing. I used a sweet chili sauce. Honestly, these were delicious and even better the second day. Will be making again!
I made these for Christmas- so easy and good.
